threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can always spot the newcomers—they're the ones still trying to figure out the bus routes instead of just embracing the night buses.
Caught a guy on the 333 arguing with his reflection in the window, convinced it was a rival. Brixton really brings out the characters at night.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the guy in an avocado suit arguing with a pigeon over bread crumbs at Hermannplatz, I thought, 'Yep, this is home.'

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous techno party in a laundromat at 3 AM, complete with spinning washers and a DJ on the countertop.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Locals know the best taco spots can have a line out the door, but the waiter's smile fades at the mention of pouring rain.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo deep in a Muni nap, drooling on his bow tie. Classic SF—always a surprise around every corner.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the vibrant murals here pop up overnight, but most are painted over carefully, some taking weeks to get just right.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still search for the right metro line on their phone, even when locals glide straight to the platform.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to stand on the left side of the escalators at Dalston Junction. Everyone knows it’s all about the right side here.
Heard a couple arguing about a missing shoe on the N109 last night. Turns out, she threw it out the window at some guy on a bike.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy in a full suit riding his bike with a giant inflatable flamingo under his arm to the canal. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Neukölln, you can find cafes that serve traditional Turkish breakfast alongside vegan brunch, all while the smell of fresh simit wafts through the air.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only true locals know to avoid 16th Street BART on weekdays after 5 PM; it’s like a rush hour Bermuda Triangle for delays and lost patience.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 this morning, and it stopped for 10 minutes to let a guy get his sax out of a bush. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can stroll into any bar and get a proper vermut, but only locals know the hidden gems that serve it on tap with the right olives.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their struggle to navigate the Gràcia's winding streets; they often look down at their phones, confused, while locals breeze by.
